newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba Red River flood 50 pct likely match worst.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba Red River flood 50 pct likely match worst.

text.p: There is an average chance flooding of the Red River Valley between Winnipeg and the U.S. border later this month will match the worst of the century, a Manitoba Natural Resources official told Reuters.

"There's a median chance this flood could be as bad as the worst one of the century and a 10 percent chance it could be 5.0 ft above last year (3.2 ft over the century's worst)," MNR's manager of Water Planning and Development Larry Whitney said.
A record breaking blizzard that dumped 57 cms of snow on the Red River over the weekend forced MNR to revise its forecast.
The Red River overflows its banks at Morris, Manitoba, half way between Winnipeg and the U.S. border, at 769.5 ft (235 m) above sea level, Whitney said.
Last year's flood reached 779.5 ft (238 m) above sea level, or 10 ft (3 m) above the flood stage and flooded 275 sq m (712 sq km) of prime farmland, delaying seeding by a month.
There was a 90 percent chance this spring's flood would reach that level, Whitney said.
The Valley's fertile soil produces wheat, barley, canola, corn and flax and accounts for two percent of Prairie acreage but 3.5 percent of output, the Canadian Wheat Board has said.

There was a median chance this spring's flood would match the peak floods of the century, set in 1950 and 1979 at Morris at 781.3 ft (238.1 m) above sea level, or 11.8 ft (3.6 m) above the flood stage when 400 sq m (1,036 sq km) of land was flooded.
The top of the flood dike at Morris was at 786 ft (240 m) above sea level and there was a 10 percent chance flood waters would rise above the dikes, Whitney said.
"The crucial thing now is the timing. They're calling for the peak at Fargo (N.D.) Friday or this weekend so that crest will arrive here in one week to 10 days," Whitney said.
More snow or rain could make it the century's worst flood.
Simultaneous cresting of the Red's tributaries could also lead to the century's worst flood, he said.
The worst flood ever believed to have occured in Manitoba's Red River Valley was in 1826 and was about six ft (two m) higher than the 1950 and 1979 floods, Whitney said.
